ثَوْبٌ فَاسِخٌ [(assumed tropical:) A faded garment: so in the language of the present day: perhaps post-classical]. (A in art. رمد.) ＝
-A2- [الفَاسِخُ is a name given by the Jews to their festival of The Passover: see De Sacy's Chrest. Ar., sec. ed., i. 291, and p. 97 of the Ar. text: and see also الفِصْحُ.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
